Class OpenSSLPreSharedKeySelector

java.lang.Object
org.apache.tomcat.util.net.openssl.OpenSSLPreSharedKeySelector
All Implemented Interfaces:
PreSharedKeySelector
public class OpenSSLPreSharedKeySelector extends Object implements PreSharedKeySelector
Callback implementation that Tomcat uses to select a pre-shared key for a given connection based on the identity provided by the client.

    • select

      public byte[] select(long ssl, String identity)
      Description copied from interface: PreSharedKeySelector
      Selects the TLSv1.2 pre-shared key on the server side given the provided client identity.
      Specified by:
      select in interface PreSharedKeySelector
      Parameters:
      ssl - the SSL instance
      identity - the PSK identity provided by the client
      Returns:
      the pre-shared key, or null if the identity is not recognized. OpenSSL limits the key to between 1 and 512 bytes long (inclusive). If the byte sequence is truly random then 16 bytes are recommended for 128-bit ciphers and 32 bytes for 256-bit ciphers.

    • select

      public byte[] select(long ssl, byte[] identity, int[] cipherSuite)
      Description copied from interface: PreSharedKeySelector
      Selects the TLSv1.3 pre-shared key and digest on the server side given the provided client identity.

      The callback is a little more complex for TLSv1.3. The return value is still the pre-shared key but OpenSSL also needs to know which digest to use. Because the OpenSSL API only exposes a cipher for this, that is what Tomcat populates the cipherSuite array with but only the digest is relevant.

      Specified by:
      select in interface PreSharedKeySelector
      Parameters:
      ssl - the SSL instance
      identity - the PSK identity provided by the client
      cipherSuite - a single-element array that must be populated with a IANA TLSv1.3 cipher suite identifier
      Returns:
      the pre-shared key (strictly the input to the KDF), or null if the identity is not recognized. OpenSSL limits the key to between 1 and 48 bytes long (inclusive). If the byte sequence is truly random then 16 bytes are recommended for 128-bit ciphers and 32 bytes for 256-bit ciphers.
